taxonomic_note: World Flora Online accepts the nominate subspecies and includes Texas in its native range. Species-level and other-infraspecific records are not transferred automatically.
look_here_first: FIRST inspect a mid-stem leaf's two surfaces and edge: S. lanceolatum generally has pliable, nonwaxy, comparatively flat leaves with diffuse or elongated lower-surface vein AREOLES, unlike S. praealtum with firmer waxy upper faces and conspicuous small isodiametric lower areoles. For subsp. lanceolatum verify outer phyllaries ~1/3–2/3 inner (not the mostly 2/3+ of subsp. hesperium) and no big leafy bract directly subtending the head. Do NOT use peduncle bract counts for a hard split; the FNA genus key conflicts with its species treatments.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays and Travis are locked under the nominate concept. Williamson evidence in the review is var. hesperium and is not counted toward subsp. lanceolatum.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use growth form, leaf shape, panicle architecture, and infraspecific characters together; species-level white aster appearance is not enough for subspecies assignment.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. praealtum shows firm, waxy often rolled-margin leaves and clear small regular vein areoles below; S. lanceolatum generally pliable nonwaxy flat leaves and faint/elongate areoles. FNA GENUS key says praealtum 1–3 vs lanceolatum 5–12+ bracts, but FNA SPECIES descriptions say reverse; don't teach bract count as exclusive. Nominate subspecies needs outer/inner phyllary ratio confirmation and provenance (hesperium has long outer phyllaries and leafy head bracts).
